description: Experiment 01: supervised seven-class language identification baselines (official fastText supervised classifier vs character TF-IDF + multinomial logistic regression) on the frozen Dataset V1, with group-disjoint development roles, post-hoc temperature calibration, abstention to und, internal test evaluation and the UD v2.18 external benchmark.

role_descriptions.train: fits every model parameter; nothing else
role_descriptions.dev_tune: hyperparameter and model-family configuration selection only
role_descriptions.dev_calib: held out from selection; fits temperature scaling and abstention thresholds
role_descriptions.test: evaluated once after the selection lock is written; never used for any choice

strict.name: ud_strict_garrusi
strict.title: STRICT external benchmark: UD v2.18 Southern Kurdish (Garrusi), Latin orthography
strict.selection: strict_external is true and exclusion_reasons is empty

exploratory.name: ud_exploratory_kurmanji
exploratory.title: EXPLORATORY — prior repository exposure: UD v2.18 Northern Kurdish (Kurmanji)
exploratory.selection: strict_external is false and the only exclusion reason is legacy_ud_prior_repository_exposure; records that also overlap canonical sources are dropped

notes: thread=1 makes Hogwild SGD sequential so the trained model is deterministic for a fixed seed.

Training requires the official fasttext 0.9.2 release: 0.9.3 allocates the input matrix with posix_memalign (uninitialized) and initializes only thread/10 of it, so thread=1 runs differ between identical calls and can diverge to NaN. With thread=1, 0.9.2 initializes the first tenth of input rows uniformly and the rest to zero (deterministic upstream behaviour).
softmax is used instead of hierarchical softmax: with seven labels the full softmax is cheap and yields a proper distribution over all labels, which calibration and abstention need.
fastText autotune is not used: its objective is not macro-F1, it is multi-threaded and time-budgeted (non-deterministic), and an explicit grid scored by the shared evaluator on dev_tune is auditable.
lowercase=false and strip_accents=null keep exactly the project's conservative normalization (NFC + whitespace) so both model families see identical input and no Unicode distinction is folded.
class_weight='balanced' is searched because the primary metric is macro-F1 and sdh (8,665 train records) is the smallest class.
lbfgs on the sparse CSR matrix optimises the multinomial loss without densifying the features.

calibration.adopt_if: cross-fitted dev_calib log loss improves on raw probabilities

abstention.objective: maximise coverage subject to selective accuracy >= target; ties broken by lower thresholds
abstention.fallback: if no grid point reaches the target, choose the highest selective accuracy with coverage >= minimum_coverage
